$comment: P69 (lane `cs`, D-C-A-COMPOUND-LITERAL-IS-ITS-INITIALIZERS-VALUE-NOT-AN-OBJECT, the design audit's M1 pin): TWO compilation units, each with file-scope compound literals of the same shapes, merged into one program. The MIR tier mints each static unnamed object a nameless internal symbol through the string-literal allocator (`mintSyntheticGlobalSymbol`), and the cross-unit merge must keep all of them apart — never collide two nameless symbols, never fold one literal into its twin (they are not const, C 6.5.2.5p6 lets only const literals share). A write to one unit's object must leave the other's alone. The C meaning is ordinary (distinct static objects); the reference compilers were measured on the one-unit equivalent with the statics renamed, through `dssharness run probe-reference-cc` (it compiles one source): gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 at -std=c17 -pedantic-errors and -std=c2x (run 20260930-222707-5281cab3) and MSVC 19.51 /std:clatest (20260930-222734-2b3c832b) all exit 42. The release arm is REPORT-ONLY.
